CHAPTER 1
PROJECT DESCRIPTION
INTRODUCTION
The purpose of this impact statement is to describe reasonable projections of the environmental effects of developing Crow Tribal coal resources on two tracts of land presently under lease to Westmoreland Resources. This statement studies probable effects of coal development on a leasehold totalling approximately 30,876 acres within the Crow Ceded Area (See Map No. I-1). It does not address any site-specific mining and reclamation plan. Primary consideration is given to the rates and levels of development as stipulated in the Amended Leases between the Crow Tribe and Westmoreland Resources; a hypothetical high level of development and the possible consequences of energy conversion are also addressed.
The study was undertaken to bring the Department of the Interior into compliance with the 9th U.S. Court of Appeals opinion of June 19, 1975, and a U.S. District Court Order for the District of Montana, Billings Division, dated January 20, 1976, which in part held that the Secretary of the Interior's approval of coal leases covering approximately 30,876 acres in Montana, constituted "Major Federal Action" requiring a comprehensive environmental impact statement as well as impact statements for each separate mining plan (Cady vs. Morton, CV-74-12-BLG.). This environmental statement covering these leases will serve as the primary documentary basis upon which the Secretary of the Interior must reconsider his approval of the leases. Appendix A contains the entire U.S.D.C. order CV-74-12-BLG.
